context:
Goal: the 211 archived session handoffs stop piling up, and every open item in them gets one home (your words at 11:22 CST: let the handoffs pile in until the collector's archive work is finished; it has finished now).
Problem (cannot undo): the cull drops handoffs from the ledger and changes 135 roadmap steps marked doing, so it needs your word first.
Based on (read): the collector archived 256 sessions, and 211 of them left a handoff on the archive branch for today's handoffs; 135 roadmap steps marked doing still point at those handoffs.
Departs from: main (each archived session's handoff is its own file, and no list joins them) — a script culls the handoffs whose work is merged or done, then Haiku agents merge each group into one line per open item, in one ledger file on the collector branch; the original files stay.
Meanwhile: the coordinator waits; nothing starts before your yes.

options.gain: One ledger lists every open item from the archived sessions, so nothing in them is lost and the 135 doing steps can be sorted.
options.how: A script culls the handoffs whose work is merged or done; Haiku agents merge each group into one line per open item, in one ledger file on the collector branch; the originals are kept.
options.label: Yes, go as planned
options.lose: A Haiku merge can word an item less exactly than its handoff did; the originals stay for a check.

options.gain: The cleanup runs the way you want it.
options.how: Write what to change in the note; the coordinator re-plans.
options.label: Change the plan
options.lose: It waits until you say what to change.

Your later open-PR sort answer (12:44 CST, "pass 2 should be a haiku workflow, and pass 3 can be a sonnet reviewer on the close verdicts") also needs no page item. title: Go for step one of the handoff cleanup: cull the handoffs whose work landed, then merge the rest into one ledger?
why: It keeps every original, so a wrong merge can be checked against its source, and it ends with one list to work from.
